title: Inner-anodyne attachment of one coarse-groupoid edge
statement:
Use simplicial sets, their nerves and horns from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a finite set $A$, let $\mathcal I_A$ be the ordinary category with object set $A$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair of objects, and put $G_A=N(\mathcal I_A)$. Thus $(G_A)_m=A^{m+1}$, with operators selecting or repeating entries. An inner-anodyne map means a member of the smallest class of simplicial maps containing every inner horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$ with $0<i<m$ and closed under pushouts, transfinite composition and retracts. For every nonempty finite set $A$, vertex $a\in A$ and element $b\notin A$, the canonical map of simplicial sets
$$G_A\amalg_{G_{\{a\}}}G_{\{a,b\}}\longrightarrow G_{A\cup\{b\}}$$
is inner anodyne. The pushout here is formed degree by degree in sets.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof: the three nested filtrations proving that the coarse-nerve inclusion is inner anodyne; relabel the pivot as N. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $C=A\setminus\{a\}$, $B=A\cup\{b\}$ and $K=G_A\cup G_{\{a,b\}}\subseteq G_B$. In every degree the two subsets intersect in the single constant word at $a$, which is $(G_{\{a\}})_m$. Thus their degreewise pushout is exactly $K$, compatibly with every operator. Its words are precisely those not containing both $b$ and an element of $C$. If $C$ is empty, $K=G_B$ and the assertion is the empty composite of horn attachments. Henceforth allow $C\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: A word is degenerate exactly when two adjacent entries agree: a degeneracy repeats an entry, and any adjacent repetition can be removed by that degeneracy. Compressing each maximal constant run gives a unique nondegenerate word, together with the unique monotone surjection recording its run lengths. The compressed word is also a face of the original word, obtained by selecting one position in each maximal run. Since a simplicial subset is closed under faces and degeneracies, a word belongs to it if and only if its compressed word does. In particular all vertices already belong to $K$.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: For a nondegenerate word $w$ outside $K$, erase its occurrences of $a$, and colour the remaining letters by $L$ for $C$ and $R$ for $b$. Both colours occur. Let $\beta(w)\geq1$ count consecutive colour changes in this erased list; choose its first colour change, with original endpoint positions $i<j$. The entries between these endpoints can only be $a$, so nondegeneracy forces $j=i+1$ or $j=i+2$; in the second case the intervening entry is $a$.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: Call the word lower when $j=i+1$, and upper when $j=i+2$. Inserting $a$ between the selected endpoints of a lower word $v$ gives an upper word $u$; deleting that intervening $a$ recovers $v$. Both words are nondegenerate because the two endpoint letters have different colours and neither is $a$. Erasing $a$ gives exactly the same list before and after this operation, so the selected change and $\beta$ are unchanged. These operations are inverse bijections between all lower and upper words outside $K$. Write $n=\dim v\geq1$, $r=\beta(v)$ and $k=i+1$ for this pair. Then $\dim u=n+1$, $1\leq r\leq n$, $d_k u=v$, and $0<k<n+1$.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: Deleting one non-$a$ letter cannot increase $\beta$: at an end it removes zero or one change; internally the decrease in the count is $\epsilon(P,X)+\epsilon(X,Q)-\epsilon(P,Q)$, which is either $0$ or $2$ for the two colours, where $\epsilon$ is $0$ on equal colours and $1$ otherwise. Deleting an $a$ leaves the erased colour list unchanged. If a resulting face is degenerate, its compressed word has dimension at most $n-1$ when the face is a face of an $(n+1)$-dimensional upper word.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: Fix a pair $(v,u)$ of rank $(n,r)$, and denote its chosen local string by $x,a,y$, with $x,y$ of opposite colours. Consider a nondegenerate face $d_\ell u$ with $\ell\ne k$ which deletes neither $x$ nor $y$. The displayed $a$ and its endpoints survive. Removing an earlier letter from a constant-colour initial portion cannot introduce an earlier colour change, and removing a later letter cannot change this first one. Thus the surviving displayed gap is still the selected gap and this face is upper. This also treats deletion of any occurrence of $a$ other than the displayed one.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: Consider instead the face deleting $x$. In the erased colour list, all letters preceding $x$ have the colour of $x$, since $(x,y)$ is the first change. If there is a preceding non-$a$ letter $z$, its colour is that of $x$, so the surviving displayed $a$ separates $z$ from $y$ at the first change: the face is upper whenever it is nondegenerate. (If another $a$ becomes adjacent to the displayed one, the face is degenerate.) If no such $z$ exists, deleting $x$ removes the initial change, so $\beta$ drops by one; the face might also fall in $K$.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: For the face deleting $y$, let $z$ be the next non-$a$ letter, if any. If $z$ has the colour of $y$, the displayed $a$ now separates $x,z$ at the first change, so a nondegenerate face is upper. If $z$ has the colour of $x$, the two consecutive colour changes through $y$ disappear and $\beta$ drops by two. If there is no $z$, the last change disappears and $\beta$ drops by one. Consecutive $a$'s created by this deletion give a degenerate face. Consequently every face $d_\ell u$ other than $v=d_k u$ is in $K$, is degenerate with compressed dimension at most $n-1$, is upper of dimension $n$, or is lower of dimension $n$ with strictly smaller $\beta$.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: Construct the attachment sequence by increasing $n\geq1$, then increasing $r=1,\ldots,n$, and then by any finite enumeration of the pairs of rank $(n,r)$. At every stage the current subset has exactly the nondegenerate words of $K$ and the two members of each already processed pair. Before dimension $n$ it also contains every nondegenerate simplex of dimension less than $n$. Initially no pair has been processed and all vertices are in $K$, so both assertions hold. In the preceding face classification, an upper $n$-simplex is the upper member of a pair whose lower dimension is $n-1$, and a lower $n$-simplex with smaller $\beta$ has already occurred at this dimension. Therefore every face of $u$ other than $v$ is in the current subset $H$. Every face of $v$ has dimension less than $n$ and is also in $H$. Adjoining $v,u$ and their degeneracies consequently gives a simplicial subset $H'$; the two designated words are not already in $H$, because the current pair is unprocessed, the pairs partition the words outside $K$, and the exact description of $H$ contains only processed pairs. The face checks show that this exact description remains valid after adjoining the current pair. After all ranks for $n$ the invariant holds for the next dimension.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: The characteristic map $\Delta^{n+1}\to G_B$ associated to $u$ sends a monotone map $\theta:[m]\to[n+1]$ to the word $u\theta$. By the horn definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $\theta$ lies outside $\Lambda_k^{n+1}$ exactly when its image contains every index other than $k$. Its image is therefore either $[n+1]$ or $[n+1]\setminus\{k\}$. Thus every simplex outside the horn maps to a run expansion of $u$ or of $v$, respectively. The horn itself maps into $H$ by the preceding face check.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: For either of these two images, a run expansion uniquely determines $\theta$: the reduced words $u,v$ have distinct adjacent entries, so their successive run lengths recover the unique surjection onto the specified ordered image. The reduced words $u$ and $v$ are different and are both new in $H'$. Hence the characteristic map bijects the degree-$m$ complement of the horn with the degree-$m$ complement of $H$ in $H'$, for every $m$. The degreewise pushout $H\amalg_{\Lambda_k^{n+1}}\Delta^{n+1}$ is consequently $H'$: the horn elements are identified with their prescribed images in $H$, and all remaining elements are exactly the distinct new elements just described. These identifications commute with operators because the two maps are simplicial. This proves the attachment square directly, even when nonadjacent vertices of $u$ coincide.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching

proof.text: Each attachment is a pushout of the inner horn $\Lambda_k^{n+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{n+1}$ because $0<k<n+1$. There are finitely many words of each fixed length, since $B$ is finite, so each rank requires finitely many individual attachments; no closure under arbitrary coproducts is being assumed. The dimension/rank order gives a countable composite, with union $G_B$, since each nondegenerate word outside $K$ occurs in its unique pair. Closure under pushouts and transfinite composition in the stated definition of inner anodyne now proves $K\hookrightarrow G_B$ inner anodyne. Through the identification in step 1 this is precisely the canonical map in the statement.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.5, proof, coarse-nerve horn filtration; agent expansion with first-colour-change matching
